This book has been prepared for use with the book 
`r if (knitr::is_latex_output()) {
   'Scientific Research and Methodology,'
} else {
   '[Scientific Research and Methodology](https://bookdown.org/pkaldunn/Book/),'
}`
which is an introduction to quantitative research methods in the scientific, engineering and health disciplines.

This course introduces the whole research process,
from asking a research question to analysis and reporting of the data.
The focus, however, is on the analysis of data.





## Answers to questions {-}

The answers to most of the **Optional** tutorial questions 
are given in App.&nbsp;\@ref(OptionalAnswers).

Some answers are implied by working through the online exercises.
Tutors have answers to almost all questions.






## Statistical software {-}

Most of this book can be read without relying on any specific statistical software.
However,
some parts explicitly mention and refer to [jamovi](https://www.jamovi.org/) 
[@Software:jamovi]
and/or
[SPSS](https://www.ibm.com/products/spss-statistics)
[@Software:SPSS].

jamovi is *free* and is like (but not exactly the same as) SPSS:

> jamovi is a new '3rd generation' statistical spreadsheet. 
> designed from the ground up to be easy to use, 
> jamovi is a compelling alternative 
> to costly statistical products such as SPSS and SAS.
>
> --- From the jamovi homepage (https://www.jamovi.org/)







## Icons used on this book {-}

The icons used in this book have meanings; for example:

```{block2, type="rmdobjectives"}
These chunks introduce the objectives for the chapters of the book.
```



```{block2, type="rmdimportant"}
These chunks highlight common mistakes or warnings, about (for example) a particular concept or about using a formula.
```



```{block2, type="rmdtip"}
These chunks offer helpful information.
```


```{block2, type = "rmdVideoSolution"}
This icon flags questions tat have *video solutions* in the online book:
A narrator works through the question, explaining the solution.
```




## How this book was made {-}

This book was made using
**R**
[@Software:Rsoftware],
and the **bookdown** package
[@Software:Rbookdown],
which is based on [Markdown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Markdown) syntax,
using **knitr**
[@package:knitr].
Numerous other **R** packages were used too:

* The diagrams were made in base **R**,
  or using the **diagram** package [@Rpackage:diagram].
* The **kableExtra** package was used for nicer tables
  [@package:kableExtra].
* The map in Sect. \@ref(SamplingParking) (interactive in the online version) is made using the **leaflet** package [@package:leaflet].
* Some data tables in the online version are displayed using the **DT** package
  [@package:DT].
* Some plots use the **plotrix** package
  [@package:plotrix].
* The NHANES data is provided by the **NHANES** package
  [@data:NHANES:Rpackage].
* Some data are from the **GLMsData** package
  [@computing:GLMsData:Rpackage].
* The **viridis** package is used for some colour specifications
  [@package:viridis] to make colours easier for those with colour-blindess to distinguish colours,
  and for better greyscale printing.
* The **webex** package was used to create the interactive web exercises
  [@package:webex].

All of this software is *free* and open source.

Other resources used include:

* The online quizzes are embedded using [H5P](https://h5p.org) iframes.
* Icons are from [**iconmonstr**](https://iconmonstr.com/) 
  and are freely available.
* The text folding (in the online version) was implemented by adapting advice
  from [StackOverflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/53810294/folding-general-text-in-r-bookdown).
* The polling in the online book is provided by [Ferendum](https://www.ferendum.com/en/).
* The cover for the book was made using a free image with [Canva](https://www.canva.com/).

## Learning Outcomes {-}

	
In this book,
you will learn to:


* Develop quantitative research questions and testable hypotheses.
* Design quantitative studies to answer simple quantitative research questions.
* Select and produce appropriate graphical, numerical and statistical analyses.
* Select, apply and interpret the results of the correct statistical technique to analyse data.
* Comprehend, apply and communicate in the language of research and statistics.
* Demonstrate professional integrity in planning, interpreting and reporting the results of quantitative studies.
